<p>JPG (Joint Photographic Experts Group), is a universal file format that utilizes an algorithm to compress photographs and graphics. The considerable compression that JPG offers is the reason for its wide use. As such, the relatively small size of JPG files makes them excellent for transporting over the Internet and using on websites. You can use our <a href="https://www.freeconvert.com/compress-jpeg" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">compress JPEG</a><span style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: 400;"> tool to reduce the file size by up to 80%!</span></p>
<p> </p>
<p>If you need even better compression, you can convert <a href="https://www.freeconvert.com/jpg-to-webp" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">JPG to WebP</a>, which is a newer and more compressible file format.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2>How to open a JPG file?</h2>
<p>Almost all image-viewer programs and applications recognize and can open JPG files. Simply double-clicking the JPG file will usually result in its opening in your default image viewer, image editor, or web browser. To select a specific application to open the file, utilize right-click, and select "Open with" to make your selection.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>JPG files open automatically on popular web browsers such as Chrome, Microsoft applications such as Microsoft Photos, and Mac OS applications such as Apple Preview. To resize JPEG images use our Image Resizer tool.</p>
<p> </p>
<p><b>Developed by:</b> <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Photographic_Experts_Group" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Joint Photographic Experts Group</a></p>
<p><b>Initial Release:</b> 18 September 1992</p>

<p>WebP is an open-source file type that uses <a href="https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/compression" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">predictive compression</a> to create images that are ideal for web pages and mobile applications. WebP images are as much as 30 percent smaller than <a href="https://www.lifewire.com/jpg-jpeg-file-4139913" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">JPEG (JPG)</a> and <a href="https://www.file-extensions.org/png-file-extension" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Portable Network Graphics (PNG)</a> files, with similar visual quality. WebP images load quickly on web pages and mobile applications.</p>
<h2>How to open a WebP file?</h2>
<p>The default program for opening WebP is Google Chrome (Chrome), which works across platforms. WebP files also open automatically on GIMP and Microsoft Paint. Besides Chrome, all other web browsers support the WebP format.</p>
<p>Alternative viewers include Pixelmator and Photopea. Also, try Corel PaintShop Pro. IrfanView, Windows Photo Viewer, and Adobe Photoshop each require a WebP plugin. </p>
<p><strong>Developed by:</strong> Google</p>
<p><strong>Initial Release:</strong> September 2010</p> <p><a href="https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/compression" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Google Developer article on WebP compression</a></p>
<p><b>Related WebP Tools: </b></p>
